2. L-System Morphogenesis & Differential Growth Engine
The macro-structure of the organogram is driven by a parametric Lindenmayer System (L-System) designed to yield organic, root-and-branch topologies. The system state is updated via differential operators modulated by scaling variables φ and ψ.

plete="true">State Variables:
  • φ: The fundamental scaling ratio dictating branch deceleration.
  • ψ: The angular perturbation coefficient dictating branch tortuosity.
  • T: The continuous metric tensor representing local tissue tension, defined differentially as: 
    T=dϕdr⋅∇ϕcap T equals the fraction with numerator d phi and denominator d r end-fraction center dot nabla phi

The continuous scalar field mapping is passed through a randomized threshold distribution function

2. The Self-Referential Master Field Operator
Because the engine is entirely self-referential, the Signed Distance Field does not evaluate external primitives. Instead, the 1-bit words determine the choice of blending operator, which in turn structurally cuts and forms the Klein bottle housing those very same bits.
